status: exact factor-two sharpness and product stability established internally; arbitrary-channel dimension-free theorem and bounded-Holevo implication remain UNKNOWN

claims.statement: For every d>=2, the marginal Phi_d of the optimal symmetric universal 1-to-2 qudit cloner is self-compatible, unital, trace preserving, and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint. If an EB CPTP map Psi satisfies I-Psi <= c(I-Phi_d), then c>=2. The EB depolarizing map with traceless eigenvalue 1/(d+1) attains equality.
assumptions: Loewner order on Hermitian Hilbert-Schmidt space
claims.status: internally proved exact consequence of established universal-cloning marginal and direct isotropic-Choi overlap bound
claims.novelty_boundary: The cloning channel and universal-cloning optimum are prior work. No novelty claim is made for them. This report isolates sharpness of c=2 for the operator-order target; external review and priority remain open.
claims.costs: No acquisition or numerical precision cost. A direct Choi table has d^4 entries; covariant channel descriptions are parameterized by d and the Haar measure-and-prepare representation.
claims.falsifier: An EB depolarizing channel with parameter greater than 1/(d+1), a failure of the universal-cloner marginal parameter, or an EB comparator that violates the isotropic-overlap bound after twirling.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether c=2 suffices for non-isotropic, non-product self-compatible channels in d>=3.

claims.statement: For finite tensor products of simultaneously diagonalizable self-adjoint contractions Phi_j and EB comparators Psi_j with nonnegative eigenvalues and mu_j>=2 lambda_j-1 on each common eigenmode, the single product EB map tensor_j Psi_j satisfies I-tensor_j Psi_j <= 2(I-tensor_j Phi_j). Tensor-product broadcasters make tensor_j Phi_j self-compatible when every Phi_j is self-compatible.
assumptions: each factor has a single full-domain EB comparator satisfying its factor-two order bound
claims.status: internally proved exact scalar induction; no numerical search
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a scoped tensor-closure statement. It does not cover noncommuting factors, negative spectra, or arbitrary compatible channels.
claims.costs: A succinct repeated-factor description uses O(k) local map specifications; explicit full superoperator materialization can cost d^4 coefficients for total dimension d.
claims.falsifier: A scalar tuple in [0,1] violating the induction inequality, or failure of the stated factorwise map/broadcaster assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Apply to structured product channels only as a no-go filter for tensor amplification; look for genuinely interacting channel families.

claims.statement: Conditional on the inherited exact d=5 audit's comparator inequalities, every tensor power of its self-compatible Weyl channel has one product EB comparator satisfying the same factor-two order inequality.
assumptions: D5_AUDIT.md compatibility and interval certificates are correct
the stored channel and comparator spectra are nonnegative
tensor-product channels and maps use the usual regrouping of outputs
claims.status: tensor extension proved internally; d=5 interval certificate inherited and not rerun in this branch
claims.novelty_boundary: This only extends an existing finite d=5 repair to its tensor powers. It is not a general Weyl-channel theorem or a dimension-free proof for arbitrary channels.
claims.costs: Base: 25 algebraic probabilities, a 25x25 Q(sqrt(5)) kernel, six rational 5-vectors, and 24 interval-checked mode inequalities. Tensor extension is symbolic; full expansion scales as d^4.
claims.falsifier: A failed base compatibility identity or one of the 24 base order inequalities; either would invalidate the inherited premise.
claims.next_gate: Use the exact sequence only to reject tensor-power amplification of this restricted line-cover obstruction.
